quotes.t: You will find rest from vain fancies if you perform every act in life as though it were your last.
The first rule is to keep an untroubled spirit. The second is to look things in the face and know them for what they are.
Let men see, let them know, a real man, who lives as he was meant to live.
The lion who breaks the enemy's ranks is a minor hero compared to the lion who overcomes himself.
Fortunate is he who does not carry envy as a companion.
Come, seek, for search is the foundation of fortune: every success depends upon focusing the heart.
The Superior Man is all-embracing and not partial. The inferior man is partial and not all-embracing.
Be loyal and trustworthy. Do not befriend anyone who is lower than yourself in this regard. When making a mistake, do not be afraid to correct it.
The scholar who cherishes the love of comfort is not fit to be deemed a scholar.
Know satisfaction and you shall not be imperiled; then you will long endure.
A good traveler has no fixed plans and is not intent upon arriving.
The Tao nourishes by not forcing. By not dominating, the Master leads.
The man who renounces himself, comes to himself.
It was a high counsel that I once heard given to a young person — 'Always do what you are afraid to do.'
The ancestor of every action is a thought.
Once a brother, always a brother, no matter the distance, no matter the difference, and no matter the issue.
The finest memories are those where we have helped someone without expecting anything in return.
Give your love to all, trust in the team to which you are joined, and do not do wrong to others for your own self-gratification.
An old maxim says that a professional writer is an amateur who didn't quit.
Nothing happens by chance, my friend... No such thing as luck.
If it's never our fault, we can't take responsibility for it. If we can't take responsibility for it, we'll always be its victim.
Reason well from the beginning and then there will never be any need to look back with confusion and doubt.
Human happiness and human satisfaction must ultimately come from within oneself. It is wrong to expect some final satisfaction to come from money or from a computer.
When you engage in fulfilling the needs of others, your own needs are fulfilled as a by-product.
A happy man is too satisfied with the present to dwell too much on the future.
The important thing is not to stop questioning; curiosity has its own reason for existing.
Few people are capable of expressing with equanimity opinions that differ from the prejudices of their social environment.
If you believe it will work out, you'll see opportunities. If you believe it won't, you will see obstacles.
You are not stuck where you are unless you decide to be.
You leave old habits behind by starting out with the thought, 'I release the need for this in my life.'
Whatever the mind of man can conceive and believe, it can achieve. Thoughts are things!
Do not wait; the time will never be just right. Start where you stand, and work with whatever tools you may have at your command, and better tools will be found as you go along.
In planning to acquire your share of the riches, let no one influence you to scorn the dreamer.
There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.
To be, or not to be: that is the question.
How far that little candle throws his beams! So shines a good deed in a naughty world.
Men are disturbed, not by things, but by the principles and notions which they form concerning things.
Don't demand that things happen as you wish, but wish that they happen as they do happen, and you will go on well.
Practice yourself, for heaven's sake, in little things; from them proceed to greater.
Love possesses not nor would it be possessed; for love is sufficient unto love.
Faith is an oasis in the heart which will never be reached by the caravan of thinking.
Half of what I say is meaningless; but I say it so that the other half may reach you.
The present moment is filled with joy and happiness. If you are attentive, you will see it.
When you begin to see that your enemy is suffering, that is the beginning of insight.
People usually consider walking on water or in thin air a miracle. But I think the real miracle is not to walk either on water or in thin air, but to walk on earth.
To think is easy. To act is hard. But the hardest thing in the world is to act in accordance with your thinking.
We are shaped and fashioned by what we love.
To be pleased with one's limits is a wretched state.
Let me not pray to be sheltered from dangers, but to be fearless in facing them. Let me not beg for the stilling of my pain, but for the heart to conquer it.
Death is not extinguishing the light; it is only putting out the lamp because the dawn has come.
When old words die out on the tongue, new melodies break forth from the heart; and where the old tracks are lost, new country is revealed with its wonders.
Don't get set into one form, adapt it and build your own, and let it grow, be like water.
There are no limits. There are plateaus, but you must not stay there, you must go beyond them.
Use only that which works, and take it from any place you can find it.
Our lack of confidence is not the result of difficulty. The difficulty comes from our lack of confidence.
Associate with people who are likely to improve you.
No man is good by chance. Virtue is something which must be learned.
Government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the Earth.
If we never try, we shall never succeed.
You cannot fail, if you resolutely determine that you will not.
Man is by nature a social animal.
Try to be a rainbow in someone's cloud.
Non-violence is the greatest force at the disposal of mankind.
We shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight on the landing grounds, we shall fight in the fields and in the streets, we shall fight in the hills; we shall never surrender.
To love oneself is the beginning of a lifelong romance.
Do the right thing. It will gratify some people and astonish the rest.
How am I going to live today in order to create the tomorrow I'm committed to?
One can never consent to creep when one feels an impulse to soar.
The art of war is of vital importance to the State.
Today is victory over yourself of yesterday; tomorrow is your victory over lesser men.
When an inner situation is not made conscious, it happens outside, as fate.
The more you praise and celebrate your life, the more there is in life to celebrate.
Small aim is a crime; have great aim.
The world is the great gymnasium where we come to make ourselves strong.
Yesterday is gone. Tomorrow has not yet come. We have only today. Let us begin.
Where the spirit does not work with the hand, there is no art.
Justice without force is powerless; force without justice is tyrannical.
A woman is like a tea bag; you never know how strong it is until it's in hot water.
Change is inevitable. Change is constant.
No one is born hating another person because of the color of his skin, or his background, or his religion.
Art is a lie that makes us realize truth.
The higher we soar, the smaller we appear to those who cannot fly.
Imagine all the people living life in peace.
To love or have loved, that is enough.
Everything considered, a determined soul will always manage.
Today you are You, that is truer than true. There is no one alive who is Youer than You.
There is a place where the sidewalk ends and before the street begins.
Nobody has the power to take two steps together; you can take only one step at a time.
Making money is happiness, but making other people happy is super-happiness.

Every man's foremost task is the actualization of his unique, unprecedented and never-recurring potentialities, and not the repetition of something that another, and be it even the greatest, has already achieved.
Whether women are better than men I cannot say, but I can say they are certainly no worse.
Poverty is not just a lack of money; it is not having the capability to realize one's full potential as a human being.
I have come not to teach but to awaken. Understand therefore that I lay down no precepts.
Do not be small minded. Do not pray for gourds and pumpkins from God, when you should be asking for pure love and pure knowledge to dawn within every heart.
A computer would deserve to be called intelligent if it could deceive a human into believing that it was human.
Every body perseveres in its state of being at rest or of moving uniformly straight forward, except insofar as it is compelled to change its state by forces impressed.
Nothing happens, nobody comes, nobody goes, it's awful.
Life and death appeared to me ideal bounds, which I should first break through, and pour a torrent of light into our dark world.
Better pass boldly into that other world, in the full glory of some passion, than fade and wither dismally with age.
There is no happiness like that of being loved by your fellow-creatures, and feeling that your presence is an addition to their comfort.

A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.bio: Indian aerospace scientist and the 11th President of India (2002-2007), known as the 'Missile Man of India'.

Abraham Lincoln.bio: 16th president of the United States (1861-1865), who led the country through the Civil War and abolished slavery.

Alan Turing.bio: English mathematician and father of computer science; cracked the Enigma code in WWII.

Albert Camus.bio: French-Algerian writer and philosopher, author of The Stranger; Nobel Prize in Literature 1957.

Albert Einstein.bio: German-born theoretical physicist who developed the theory of relativity, one of the pillars of modern physics. He won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for his explanation of the photoelectric effect.
Albert Einstein.credit: Photograph by Orren Jack Turner, Princeton, N.J. Modified with Photoshop by PM_Poon and later by Dantadd., Public domain

Amartya Sen.bio: Indian economist and Nobel laureate (1998) known for work on welfare economics and famine.

Aristotle.bio: Greek philosopher and student of Plato; founder of logic and many scientific fields.

Benjamin Disraeli.bio: British statesman who served twice as Prime Minister and led the Conservative Party. He was also a successful novelist, writing books such as Coningsby and Sybil.

Blaise Pascal.bio: French mathematician, physicist and philosopher, author of the Pensées.
Blaise Pascal.credit: unknown; a copy of the painting of François II Quesnel, which was made for Gérard Edelinck en 1691, Public domain

Bruce Lee.bio: Bruce Lee was a Hong Kong-American martial artist and actor who transformed martial-arts cinema with films such as Enter the Dragon. His philosophy of adaptability — 'be water' — blended Taoist ideas with his own Jeet Kune Do.

Carl Jung.bio: Swiss psychiatrist who founded analytical psychology. His concepts of the collective unconscious, archetypes and introversion and extraversion remain influential in psychology and culture.

Charlotte Brontë.bio: English novelist, author of Jane Eyre.

Confucius.bio: Chinese philosopher whose teachings in the Analects shaped East Asian ethics, education, and governance for two millennia.

Dalai Lama.bio: The 14th Dalai Lama, spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism; Nobel Peace Prize laureate (1989), based in Dharamshala, India.

Dr. Seuss.bio: Theodor Seuss Geisel, known as Dr. Seuss, American children's author and illustrator of more than 60 books, including The Cat in the Hat, Green Eggs and Ham and How the Grinch Stole Christmas!

Eleanor Roosevelt.bio: Eleanor Roosevelt was the longest-serving First Lady of the United States, from 1933 to 1945, and reinvented the role as a platform for civil rights and social reform. Afterward she became a US delegate to the United Nations and chaired the commission that drafted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

Epictetus.bio: Epictetus was a Greek-born slave in Rome who won his freedom and became one of the most influential Stoic teachers. His Discourses and the handbook known as the Enchiridion teach that freedom lies in mastering one's own judgments and desires.

Friedrich Nietzsche.bio: German philosopher known for Thus Spoke Zarathustra and the concept of the will to power.

Golda Meir.bio: Israel's fourth Prime Minister (1969-1974) and one of its founding leaders.

Helen Keller.bio: American author and activist who, deaf and blind from childhood, became a renowned advocate for disability rights.
Helen Keller.credit: Los Angeles Times; restored by User:Rhododendrites, Public domain

Isaac Newton.bio: English physicist and mathematician who formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation.

James Joyce.bio: Irish novelist, author of Ulysses, a landmark of modernist literature.

Johann Wolfgang von Goethe.bio: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was a German writer, poet, playwright and natural philosopher, regarded as Germany's greatest literary figure. His works include the drama Faust, The Sorrows of Young Werther and Wilhelm Meister's Apprenticeship.

John Lennon.bio: English singer-songwriter, co-founder of the Beatles and solo artist known for Imagine.

Kahlil Gibran.bio: Lebanese-American writer and poet, best known for The Prophet (1923), one of the best-selling books of all time.

Lao Tzu.bio: Ancient Chinese philosopher traditionally credited with the Tao Te Ching, the foundational text of Taoism. His historicity is debated by scholars.

Leonardo da Vinci.bio: Leonardo da Vinci was an Italian Renaissance painter, engineer and anatomist whose notebooks reveal an insatiable curiosity about nature and art. He painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, and filled thousands of pages with studies, inventions and observations.

Mahatma Gandhi.bio: Leader of India's nonviolent independence movement; pioneered satyagraha and became the father of the Indian nation.

Marcus Aurelius.bio: Roman emperor and Stoic philosopher, author of the Meditations.

Mark Twain.bio: American writer (Samuel Clemens) known for Adventures of Huckleberry Finn and The Adventures of Tom Sawyer.

Martin Buber.bio: Austrian-Israeli philosopher known for I and Thou and his philosophy of dialogue.

Mary Shelley.bio: English novelist, author of Frankenstein, a founding work of science fiction.

Maya Angelou.bio: American poet and memoirist best known for I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings (1969).
Maya Angelou.credit: Bee Photos by Ryan Marty, Public domain

Meher Baba.bio: Indian spiritual master whose mantra 'Don't worry, be happy' became globally famous.
Meher Baba.credit: Central News (Agence photographique). Agence photographique pour le document reproduit (commanditaire)

Miyamoto Musashi.bio: Legendary Japanese swordsman, undefeated in over sixty duels, author of The Book of Five Rings and the Dokkodo.

Mother Teresa.bio: Albanian-Indian Catholic nun who founded the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata; Nobel Peace Prize laureate (1979).
Mother Teresa.credit: John Mathew Smith & www.celebrity-photos.com from Laurel  Maryland, USA, CC BY-SA 2.0

Muhammad Yunus.bio: Bangladeshi economist who pioneered microcredit through Grameen Bank; Nobel Peace Prize laureate (2006).

Napoleon Hill.bio: Napoleon Hill was an American self-help author best known for Think and Grow Rich (1937), one of the best-selling books of its kind. His work popularized the idea that success follows from definite purpose and a positive mental attitude.

Nelson Mandela.role: Anti-apartheid leader, President of South Africa
Nelson Mandela.bio: South African anti-apartheid revolutionary who spent 27 years in prison and became the country's first Black president in 1994.

Oprah Winfrey.bio: American talk-show host and media executive whose long-running show made her one of the most influential broadcasters in history.
Oprah Winfrey.credit: US Embassy South Africa, Public domain

Oscar Wilde.bio: Irish playwright, poet and author of The Picture of Dorian Gray, famed for his wit and epigrams.
Oscar Wilde.credit: Napoleon Sarony (restoration by Adam Cuerden), Public domain

Osho.bio: Indian mystic and spiritual teacher known for provocative discourses on meditation, love, and freedom.

Pablo Picasso.bio: Pablo Picasso was a Spanish artist who co-founded Cubism and reinvented his style across a career of nearly eighty years. Works such as Les Demoiselles d'Avignon and Guernica made him the most famous and influential artist of the 20th century.

Rabindranath Tagore.bio: Bengali poet and polymath from India; the first non-European Nobel laureate in Literature (1913), known for Gitanjali.

Ralph Waldo Emerson.bio: Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American essayist and philosopher who led the Transcendentalist movement, arguing for self-reliance, intuition and the spiritual presence in nature. His essays 'Nature' and 'Self-Reliance' shaped American thought, and he mentored both Thoreau and Whitman.

Ramakrishna.bio: 19th-century Indian mystic of Bengal; his teachings on religious pluralism influenced modern Hindu thought.

Richard Bach.bio: Richard Bach is an American writer best known for the bestselling novella Jonathan Livingston Seagull (1970) and Illusions (1977). A former Air Force pilot, his work often combines flying with spiritual themes.

Rumi.bio: 13th-century Persian poet and Sufi mystic whose Masnavi is among the most influential works of Islamic literature.

Samuel Beckett.bio: Irish playwright and novelist, author of Waiting for Godot; Nobel Prize in Literature 1969.

Seneca.bio: Roman Stoic philosopher and statesman, author of Letters to Lucilius.

Shel Silverstein.bio: Sheldon Allan Silverstein, American writer, cartoonist and songwriter; author of the children's classics The Giving Tree, Where the Sidewalk Ends and A Light in the Attic, and writer of the Johnny Cash hit "A Boy Named Sue".

Sun Tzu.bio: Ancient Chinese general traditionally credited with The Art of War, a treatise on strategy studied worldwide for over two thousand years.

Swami Vivekananda.bio: Indian Hindu monk who introduced Vedanta and Yoga to the West; famous for his 1893 Chicago Parliament of Religions address.

Thich Nhat Hanh.bio: Vietnamese Buddhist monk and peace activist who popularized mindfulness in the West; nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize by Martin Luther King Jr.

Tony Robbins.bio: Tony Robbins is an American author, coach and motivational speaker known for bestselling books such as Unlimited Power and Awaken the Giant Within. His seminars and self-help programmes have made him one of the most prominent figures in the personal development industry.

Victor Hugo.bio: French poet and novelist, author of Les Misérables and The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.

Wayne Dyer.bio: Wayne Dyer was an American self-help author and motivational speaker whose first book, Your Erroneous Zones (1976), became one of the best-selling books of all time. He wrote more than forty books and lectured widely on self-development and spirituality.

William Shakespeare.bio: English playwright and poet, widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language; author of Hamlet and Macbeth.
William Shakespeare.credit: Attributed to John Taylor, Public domain

Winston Churchill.bio: British prime minister during the Second World War and Nobel laureate in Literature.
Winston Churchill.credit: Central Office of Information, Public domain
